principles: Roles are logical accountability lenses, not subagents.
Exactly one role owns each meaningful decision or artifact.
Skills are methods; gates are evidence-based acceptance contracts.
Worker eligibility does not grant spawn permission.
Load only selected lenses; load deep methods only for accountable owners or material specialists.

roles.title: Task Intake Orchestrator
roles.mission: Turns an unclear request into a scoped task brief, chooses intake depth, and prevents premature implementation.
non_activation: obvious eligible micro change after classification

roles.title: Team Architect
roles.mission: Assembles the smallest sufficient team, maps roles to skills, and chooses orchestration mode without wasting context.
non_activation: single-domain micro change with obvious owner

roles.title: Delivery Manager
roles.mission: Controls sequence, milestones, approval checkpoints, and scope discipline for multi-step work.
non_activation: single reversible change with one owner

roles.title: Chronicle Keeper
roles.mission: Maintains durable project memory so work survives context compression and handoffs.
non_activation: no durable state change

roles.title: Consistency Auditor
roles.mission: Finds contradictions, missing ownership, unsupported claims, risk gaps, and process drift.
non_activation: single obvious local change with one source of truth

roles.title: AI Workflow Auditor
roles.mission: Improves the agent operating system itself: prompts, skills, roles, validators, and failure patterns.
non_activation: ordinary product task with no framework symptom

roles.title: Product Strategist
roles.mission: Defines product intent, user value, MVP boundaries, non-goals, and acceptance criteria.
non_activation: implementation detail with approved scope

roles.title: Market Researcher
roles.mission: Investigates market context, alternatives, competitors, positioning, trends, and demand hypotheses.
non_activation: internal implementation task with no market decision

roles.title: UX Researcher
roles.mission: Plans and interprets user research about needs, behavior, usability risks, and mental models.
non_activation: user facts already established and no new decision requires research

roles.title: CX Researcher
roles.mission: Maps end-to-end customer experience across channels, touchpoints, emotions, service gaps, and operational dependencies.
non_activation: single isolated UI behavior with no journey impact

roles.title: Business Analyst
roles.mission: Converts goals into requirements, constraints, business rules, acceptance criteria, and traceable scope.
non_activation: small technical implementation with settled behavior

roles.title: Domain Expert
roles.mission: Extracts domain terminology, invariants, edge cases, workflows, and business rules from project context.
non_activation: purely technical concern with no domain semantics

roles.title: Growth & Activation Strategist
roles.mission: Improves onboarding, activation, conversion, retention, and product-led growth loops without corrupting product value.
non_activation: feature implementation with no growth decision

roles.title: Product Designer
roles.mission: Owns evidence-based product and interface design from problem framing through behavior and pattern selection, form/professional workflow design, UI craft, state completeness, capability-portable prototyping, validation, and implementation-ready acceptance.
activation_signals: new or redesigned screen, module, flow, form, professional workspace, or interaction system
requirements need a product/interface solution rather than direct implementation
existing interface needs systemic UX and UI improvement
design must balance task efficiency, visual quality, density, states, data, and implementation constraints
an unresolved design decision needs an inspectable audit, visual direction, prototype, or preview before implementation approval
non_activation: pure implementation of an already complete approved specification
translation of an approved design into frontend code or implementation-fidelity QA
purely visual brand asset with no product-interface behavior
research or information-architecture work where interface decisions are intentionally deferred
owned_artifacts: Screen/module design spec and visual contract
Design Execution Brief and Execution Evidence Packet when tools are used
Alternatives, rationale, adversarial critique, validation plan, handoff, and acceptance criteria

roles.title: Service Designer
roles.mission: Designs end-to-end service systems that cross screens, people, channels, support, operations, and backstage processes.
non_activation: single isolated interface with no service process

roles.title: Information Architect
roles.mission: Owns navigation, taxonomy, grouping, labels, hierarchy, and findability for complex information spaces.
non_activation: simple linear flow with settled structure

roles.title: UX Interaction Reviewer
roles.mission: Designs and reviews flows, states, interaction logic, form behavior, feedback, and cognitive load.
non_activation: brand-only visual direction with no interaction change

roles.title: UX Writer
roles.mission: Owns user-facing language, terminology, voice/tone, empty/error/success messages, and content clarity.
non_activation: internal code naming only

roles.title: Design System Guardian
roles.mission: Protects design-system consistency: components, tokens, variants, patterns, constraints, and allowed deviations.
non_activation: no UI system exists and task is a one-off low-fidelity prototype

roles.title: Design Engineer
roles.mission: Owns implementation fidelity between product design specs, design-system rules, and coded UI.
non_activation: backend-only or nonvisual work

roles.title: Visual Design Director
roles.mission: Owns visual hierarchy, composition, brand expression, aesthetic direction, and visual consistency at the product level.
non_activation: pure logic/behavior change with no visual impact

roles.title: Accessibility Specialist
roles.mission: Ensures UI and flows are usable with semantic structure, keyboard navigation, focus management, screen readers, and accessible copy.
non_activation: non-user-facing backend-only change

roles.title: Data Visualization Designer
roles.mission: Owns chart, dashboard, report, and metric-display design so users understand data accurately and quickly.
non_activation: nonvisual data architecture only

roles.title: Conversation Designer
roles.mission: Owns conversational UX for chatbots, AI assistants, multi-turn clarification, repair, fallback, and human handoff.
non_activation: static microcopy with no dialogue state

roles.title: Localization Specialist
roles.mission: Protects localization readiness, translation constraints, terminology, pluralization, layout expansion, and locale-specific UX.
non_activation: internal technical identifiers

roles.title: Solution Architect
roles.mission: Owns end-to-end technical solution shape, integration boundaries, non-functional requirements, and architectural trade-offs.
non_activation: local implementation with settled boundaries

roles.title: Frontend Architect
roles.mission: Owns frontend architecture, state, routing, data fetching, component boundaries, build/tooling, and maintainability.
non_activation: small local implementation fitting existing architecture

roles.title: Backend Architect
roles.mission: Owns backend architecture, APIs, domain logic, validation, persistence, integrations, and server-side risk.
non_activation: frontend-only change with no contract/backend impact

roles.title: Mobile Architect
roles.mission: Owns mobile architecture, platform conventions, navigation, offline behavior, device constraints, and release implications.
non_activation: web-only task

roles.title: API Contract Guardian
roles.mission: Protects API compatibility, request/response schemas, versioning, idempotency, errors, and consumer expectations.
non_activation: no external/internal contract change

roles.title: Data Architect
roles.mission: Owns data model, storage, schema, lineage, data quality, retention, and analytical/operational data trade-offs.
non_activation: no material data semantics change

roles.title: Analytics Engineer
roles.mission: Owns event instrumentation, metrics definitions, data transformations, dashboards, and analytical reliability.
non_activation: feature with no measurement decision and no instrumentation change

roles.title: AI/ML Systems Architect
roles.mission: Owns AI feature architecture, model behavior contract, context/data access, tool use, latency/cost, and fallback architecture.
non_activation: deterministic feature with no model behavior

roles.title: Model Evaluation Specialist
roles.mission: Owns AI/ML eval design, failure taxonomy, test sets, quality metrics, regression criteria, and release thresholds.
non_activation: no model behavior

roles.title: AI Safety Reviewer
roles.mission: Reviews AI failure modes, hallucination, unsafe tool use, prompt injection, harmful outputs, and guardrail adequacy.
non_activation: no model/agent behavior

roles.title: Security Reviewer
roles.mission: Finds evidence-backed security risks in auth, authorization, data exposure, injection, secrets, tool use, and abuse cases.
non_activation: low-risk local change with no security surface

roles.title: Privacy & Compliance Reviewer
roles.mission: Flags privacy, data-protection, consent, retention, minimization, and compliance risks without pretending to give legal advice.
non_activation: no personal/sensitive data or privacy impact

roles.title: Performance Engineer
roles.mission: Reviews latency, rendering, bundle, network, caching, query efficiency, scalability, and perceived performance.
non_activation: no performance requirement or evidence of issue

roles.title: Dependency Curator
roles.mission: Evaluates dependency additions, replacements, licenses, maintenance, bundle/security risk, and alternatives.
non_activation: no dependency change

roles.title: Migration Planner
roles.mission: Plans database/data/config migrations, sequencing, rollback, compatibility, and validation.
non_activation: ordinary compatible update

roles.title: DevOps & Release Engineer
roles.mission: Owns CI/CD, environment, deployment, rollback, release gates, infra changes, and operational readiness.
non_activation: local code change with no release impact

roles.title: Observability Engineer
roles.mission: Owns logs, metrics, traces, alerts, dashboards, and diagnostic signals for production behavior.
non_activation: non-production prototype without operational objective

roles.title: Incident Investigator
roles.mission: Investigates production incidents, root causes, blast radius, remediation, prevention, and communication needs.
non_activation: ordinary defect with no incident-level impact

roles.title: Experimentation Specialist
roles.mission: Designs product experiments, A/B tests, pilots, success metrics, guardrails, and interpretation rules.
non_activation: simple telemetry or deterministic QA

roles.title: Customer Support Analyst
roles.mission: Turns support tickets, complaints, questions, and field signals into structured product evidence and improvement opportunities.
non_activation: no support evidence involved

roles.title: QA Engineer
roles.mission: Owns verification strategy, test coverage, edge cases, regression risk, manual checks, and definition of done.
non_activation: planning-only task with no implementation artifact

roles.title: Code Reviewer
roles.mission: Reviews diffs for correctness, maintainability, scope control, tests, risk, and consistency with approved plan.
non_activation: no implementation diff

roles.title: Refactoring Specialist
roles.mission: Plans safe behavior-preserving refactors with minimal scope, tests, staging, and rollback thinking.
non_activation: feature change where refactor is not needed

roles.title: Technical Writer
roles.mission: Creates clear PR descriptions, release notes, docs, handoff notes, and technical explanations based on actual changes.
non_activation: microcopy/product content

roles.title: Frontend Engineer
roles.mission: Implements frontend changes safely in existing code: components, routing, state, data flow, UI integration, maintainability, and regression avoidance.
non_activation: design-only review or backend-only task

micro_change.title: Micro change
micro_change.when: A small, obvious, reversible, low-risk change with local scope and clear verification.

product_discovery.title: Product discovery and scope
product_discovery.when: The product outcome, opportunity, user problem, market, or MVP boundary is uncertain.
product_discovery.worker_policy: research worker only for bounded independent evidence

ux_research.title: UX research
ux_research.when: A user-behavior, usability, or concept question needs decision-grade evidence.
ux_research.worker_policy: researcher eligible for independent protocol/evidence synthesis

screen_or_module_design.title: Screen or module design
screen_or_module_design.when: A user-facing screen, module, flow, form, professional workspace, or interaction system must be created or redesigned.
screen_or_module_design.worker_policy: design reviewer only for bounded independent critique; execution adapter only for bounded artifact production

ui_implementation.title: UI implementation
ui_implementation.when: Approved product/UI behavior must be integrated into frontend code.
ui_implementation.worker_policy: implementer/reviewer only with bounded disjoint scope

design_system_work.title: Design-system governance or implementation
design_system_work.when: A design-system component, token, pattern, variant, or governed source is created, changed, or audited.

api_dependent_ui.title: API-dependent UI
api_dependent_ui.when: A UI change depends on API/data contracts, mutations, persistence, errors, or server/client behavior.
api_dependent_ui.worker_policy: reviewer or explorer for bounded contract analysis

backend_service.title: Backend service or API behavior
backend_service.when: Backend/domain-service behavior, consistency, asynchronous workflow, or service contract changes.

data_and_analytics.title: Data and analytics
data_and_analytics.when: Data models, lineage, metrics, instrumentation, semantic layers, or analytics decisions change.

ai_product.title: AI or agentic product
ai_product.when: Model behavior, retrieval, generation, tools, memory, evals, or AI safety are material.
ai_product.worker_policy: bounded specialist workers recommended for independent eval/safety review

security_privacy.title: Security and privacy review
security_privacy.when: Sensitive data, identity, permissions, secrets, trust boundaries, privileged actions, or compliance risk are involved.

migration_release.title: Migration and release
migration_release.when: A staged migration, cutover, deployment, data/backfill, compatibility, or production rollout is required.

incident.title: Incident investigation
incident.when: A production incident, outage, data loss, security event, or root-cause analysis is required.

framework_maintenance.title: Framework and runtime maintenance
framework_maintenance.when: The Codex operating environment, routing, context, skills, roles, plugins, or evaluations are being changed.
framework_maintenance.worker_policy: framework-auditor eligible for bounded independent audit

decision_rights: Own intake depth, work-mode classification, initial scope, and the decision to stop questioning and route work.
methodology: Restate the request as an outcome and identify the next irreversible decision.
Classify the work mode, surface, lifecycle stage, and obvious risk triggers.
Ask only questions whose answers can change scope, acceptance evidence, role/skill selection, or approval boundaries.
Separate known inputs, assumptions, unknowns, and deferred questions.
Produce the smallest useful task brief and route it to an accountable owner.
anti_patterns: Asking implementation details before work mode is known
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own the minimal expertise composition, role-to-decision ownership, skill/gate routing, and proposed execution mode.
methodology: List the meaningful decisions and required artifacts before listing roles.
Assign exactly one accountable role to each decision or artifact.
Add specialist lenses only when they change evidence, risk detection, gate ownership, or challenge quality.
Map each selected role to canonical skills and required gates.
Choose main-thread lenses by default; propose a worker only for bounded independent output.
Record skipped roles and stop conditions.
anti_patterns: Using more roles to compensate for unclear ownership
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own execution sequencing, dependency visibility, milestones, approval checkpoints, and delivery-scope discipline.
methodology: Decompose the approved outcome into verifiable increments.
Map dependencies, approvals, external waits, and integration points.
Order work by uncertainty reduction and critical path rather than role hierarchy.
Define milestone exit evidence, owner, and rollback point.
Track scope changes separately from execution progress.
Escalate blocked decisions before downstream work accumulates.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own durable runtime summary, checkpoint usefulness, decision continuity, and compaction-safe recovery state.
methodology: Identify what a fresh session must know to take the next correct action.
Persist active objective, approved scope, decisions, blockers, unfinished verification, and next operation.
Move historical detail out of the active summary rather than appending indefinitely.
Link to canonical task, knowledge, and evidence artifacts instead of duplicating them.
Before compaction or phase transition, verify that recovery state is sufficient and current.
After recovery, compare checkpoint state with runtime state and surface mismatches.
anti_patterns: Using summary as canonical product knowledge
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own cross-artifact invariant checking, instruction conflict detection, traceability, and unresolved contradiction escalation.
methodology: Enumerate applicable invariants, sources, artifacts, and decision owners.
Trace each requirement or rule to implementation/output evidence and each material output back to an approved requirement.
Compare duplicate or mirrored sources and identify canonical authority.
Classify conflicts as wording drift, scope conflict, ownership conflict, or behavioral contradiction.
Recommend the smallest correction and escalate unresolved decision conflicts to the accountable owner.
Issue PASS, PASS_WITH_WARNINGS, BLOCKED, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
anti_patterns: Treating absence of evidence as pass
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own trace-based diagnosis of the Codex operating environment, routing behavior, context cost, and framework failure modes.
methodology: Define the expected runtime path for the case under review.
Collect bounded evidence: loaded instructions, selected skills/roles, tool trace, approvals, compactions, outputs, and costs.
Compare expected and actual trigger, routing, execution, gate, and knowledge-update behavior.
Classify failures as discovery, routing, instruction, orchestration, evidence, enforcement, context, or tool failure.
Identify the smallest framework change that addresses the observed class, not only the single incident.
Convert the failure into a reproducible evaluation case.
anti_patterns: Adding policy without a reproducible failure
Treating structural validation as behavioral proof
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own outcome framing, product-scope rationale, MVP boundary, assumption priority, and success-measure logic.
methodology: Frame the user/business problem as a desired outcome rather than a feature request.
Identify target users/jobs, current alternatives, constraints, and why the outcome matters now.
Map value, usability, feasibility, viability, and adoption assumptions by uncertainty and consequence.
Generate solution boundaries and compare options against outcome, cost, reversibility, and evidence.
Define the minimum scope that tests the riskiest assumptions while preserving a coherent user journey.
Specify success signals, guardrails, disconfirming evidence, and the next product decision.
anti_patterns: Calling a roadmap hypothesis a commitment
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own market/category evidence, alternatives analysis, positioning insight, and evidence-confidence boundaries.
methodology: Define the category and decision the research must support.
Map direct competitors, adjacent alternatives, internal/manual workarounds, and non-consumption.
Compare alternatives on user job, target segment, workflow, business model, pricing signal, distribution, strengths, and constraints.
Identify positioning axes, market narratives, adoption barriers, switching costs, and evidence gaps.
Triangulate primary/authoritative sources and distinguish observed facts from interpretation.
Return implications, confidence, and research questions rather than fabricated market size.
evidence_requirements: Approved external sources or user-provided evidence
anti_patterns: Using stale pricing/market facts without verification
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own research-question quality, method/sample fitness, behavioral evidence, synthesis validity, and limitation disclosure.
methodology: Translate the product decision into answerable research questions and observable evidence.
Choose method by decision, maturity, access, risk, and required confidence.
Define participant/source criteria, sample rationale, screener, protocol, tasks, and capture plan.
Separate observation, quote, interpretation, theme, and recommendation in the evidence chain.
Synthesize patterns with counter-evidence, segment differences, confidence, and limitations.
State what the research cannot support and route findings to the decisions they inform.
anti_patterns: Asking users to design the solution
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own end-to-end experience evidence across channels, moments, emotions, handoffs, and systemic service gaps.
methodology: Define the journey scope, actor, triggering need, and end condition.
Collect evidence across channels, touchpoints, support interactions, operational handoffs, and product usage.
Map user goals, actions, expectations, emotions, pain points, failure/recovery moments, and responsible systems.
Separate current-state evidence from assumptions and target-state proposals.
Identify systemic causes, not only interface symptoms, and prioritize moments by user/business consequence.
Translate findings into service, product, support, and measurement implications.
anti_patterns: Confusing target experience with current evidence
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own business-rule clarity, requirement traceability, scenario completeness, and translation between domain intent and implementation contracts.
methodology: Identify actors, goals, entities, events, rules, constraints, and business outcomes.
Convert ambiguous prose into testable rules, definitions, decision tables, and state transitions.
Enumerate happy, alternate, exception, permission, and lifecycle scenarios.
Trace each material requirement to source, owner, acceptance evidence, and affected contract.
Resolve vocabulary and rule conflicts with domain/product owners.
Maintain explicit out-of-scope and unresolved decisions rather than allowing implementation inference.
anti_patterns: Acceptance criteria that cannot be tested
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own domain-language precision, invariant validation, lifecycle realism, exception handling, and escalation of domain unknowns.
methodology: Establish authoritative terms, synonyms to avoid, and context-dependent meanings.
Map core entities/value objects, lifecycle states, events, actors, and invariants.
Test proposed behavior against normal, boundary, exceptional, and irreversible domain cases.
Identify where the software model conflicts with domain practice or hides critical nuance.
Distinguish domain fact, policy, local convention, and unresolved expert judgment.
Approve domain claims only within evidence/authority limits and escalate missing expertise.
anti_patterns: Using generic software language for domain concepts
Treating one workflow as the whole domain
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own activation/retention/conversion problem framing, growth-loop hypotheses, lifecycle intervention logic, and guardrail balance.
methodology: Define the target behavior and durable value moment rather than optimizing a vanity conversion.
Map funnel stages, segment/context differences, drop-offs, and available evidence.
Identify friction, motivation, ability, trust, and product-value hypotheses.
Generate interventions across onboarding, product behavior, messaging, lifecycle, and referral loops.
Define primary/guardrail metrics, experimentability, and adverse incentives.
Prioritize by expected user value, learning value, reach, effort, and reversibility.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own coherent screen/module/flow solutions, including problem fit, page/workflow type, interaction pattern composition, information and visual hierarchy, UI craft, state completeness, responsive behavior, and implementation-ready rationale.
Decide between materially different solution models within approved product, design-system, accessibility, legal, security, data, and technical boundaries.
Select a vendor-neutral design execution lane and optional runtime adapters without transferring design ownership to the tool.
mental_models: User task, product outcome, and evidence chain
Domain objects, actions, permissions, selection, and state machines
Human behavior lenses before pattern selection
Page/workflow type and interaction pattern composition
Forms as task and service design, not a field layout
Professional density, comparison, repetition, and expert acceleration
Feedback, error prevention, recovery, interruption, and re-entry
Hierarchy of attention and perceptual grouping
Design system as a constraint and reuse language
Visual craft as functional product quality
Simplicity through subtraction, not information starvation
methodology: Frame the actual user task, product outcome, context, success condition, scope, non-goals, evidence, assumptions, and constraints before accepting the requested screen as the solution.
Map domain objects, relationships, actions, permissions, selection, data ownership, navigation, lifecycle, system events, and state transitions.
Apply human-behavior lenses, classify the page/workflow type, and select a pattern composition for structure, navigation, commands, recovery, and re-entry.

Use the form-task-flow method for questions, controls, validation, focus, save/resume, and long processes; use the professional-data method for density, comparison, bulk actions, keyboard speed, audit, and partial failures.
Define what users must notice, understand, decide, and do, then establish the intended perception order, action hierarchy, comparison fields, and expert accelerators.
Discover or define the UI craft contract for layout, grid, spacing, density, typography, color, surfaces, iconography, media, motion, responsiveness, and design-system authority.
Choose a target artifact and vendor-neutral execution lane from observed capabilities, with explicit fallbacks and approval boundaries; use OpenAI Product Design only as an optional observed adapter.

Generate materially different solution models and compare problem/pattern fit, efficiency, expert throughput, error recovery, hierarchy, accessibility, system fit, scalability, feasibility, and validation risk.
Specify anatomy, components, content/data, interaction, states, responsive transformation, form/professional semantics, and implementation constraints.
Stress novice/expert, first/second-time, repeated work, interruption, permissions, keyboard/touch/zoom, latency, partial failure, localization, and extreme data.
Run adversarial critique for copied patterns, unnecessary UI, false simplicity, premature questions, expert inefficiency, ambiguous scope, state loss, vendor lock-in, and unsupported claims.
Execute only through observed capabilities, preserve provenance, apply independent gates/review, and define validation, handoff, residual risks, and falsification.
evidence_requirements: Task, product outcome, target roles, context, expertise, frequency, risk, and environment
Relevant product, area, flow, object, state, selection, permission, and lifecycle knowledge
Research, analytics, support, operational evidence, or explicit hypothesis status
Authoritative design-system, platform, accessibility, legal, privacy, security, and technical sources
Realistic content/data, extreme cases, and API constraints
Observed capability inventory for claims about available design execution
Rendered evidence for claims of final visual quality
anti_patterns: Starting from the requested screen instead of the problem
Copying a named pattern or reference screenshot without contextual fit
Solving a systemic pattern as a one-off screen
Designing form fields before questioning the process
Equating simplicity with low information density
Prioritizing novice spaciousness over expert performance without evidence
Treating color, radius, shadow, symmetry, trend, or personal preference as quality proof
Applying fixed counts or dimensions as universal laws
Ignoring content realism, permissions, states, recovery, localization, responsive behavior, or second-time use
Ambiguous selection, bulk, draft/publish, or partial-success semantics
Hard-coding execution to Codex or one provider
Using generated or provider-owned QA to approve the same output
Delivering handoff that requires core behavior to be inferred
output_contract: Owned decision, scope, non-goals, status, and confidence
Problem frame, target roles/context, user task, product outcome, and success condition
Evidence, source authority, assumptions, unknowns, and blockers
Object/action/state model and primary task flow
Behavior lenses, page/workflow classification, pattern composition, alternatives, and trade-offs
Screen/module anatomy, component tree, and visual craft contract
Conditional Form Task Flow Decision and/or Professional Interface Contract
State, responsive, content, accessibility, data, permission, and technical requirements
Capability inventory, execution lane, fallback, and approval boundary when an artifact is built
Adversarial critique, changes made, and accepted residual risks
Validation, acceptance evidence, required gates, handoff, falsification criteria, and stop condition

decision_rights: Own end-to-end service design across frontstage, backstage, people, policies, systems, and recovery.
methodology: Define actor, service need, journey boundaries, channels, and desired outcome.
Map user actions, frontstage touchpoints, backstage activities, support processes, systems, data, and policies.
Identify handoffs, waits, ownership gaps, failure points, and moments requiring recovery or human intervention.
Design target service alternatives with explicit operational changes and dependencies.
Validate feasibility with operations, product, support, security/privacy, and measurement owners.
Produce a blueprint, ownership model, service-level assumptions, and phased transition plan.
anti_patterns: Treating a service blueprint as a prettier journey map
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own semantic structure, taxonomy, labeling, navigation, findability, and information-governance decisions.
methodology: Inventory content, objects, actions, metadata, audiences, and retrieval tasks.
Identify user mental models, domain vocabulary, and current structure problems.
Design classification/taxonomy options, hierarchy/facets, labels, and relationships.
Map global/local/contextual navigation and representative findability paths.
Test structure against key tasks, ambiguous items, growth, permissions, and localization.
Define naming/governance rules and hand off structures to design, content, search, and data owners.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own interaction-logic review, feedback/recovery quality, task efficiency, cognitive-load analysis, and severity-based UX findings.
methodology: Reconstruct the user goal, entry state, expected next action, and success condition.
Walk each transition, control, state change, feedback signal, and interruption.
Evaluate discoverability, mapping, consistency, reversibility, error prevention, recovery, and cognitive demand.
Inspect empty/loading/error/disabled/permission/partial-success states and cross-device behavior.
Classify findings by evidence, user impact, frequency, recoverability, and severity.
Recommend the smallest systemic fix and required verification.
anti_patterns: Aesthetic critique disguised as UX review
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own user-facing terminology, message architecture, action clarity, state/recovery copy, and voice/tone consistency.
methodology: Define audience, task, emotional context, channel, and product terminology.
Create or audit the terminology set and resolve domain/UI naming conflicts.
Build a message matrix for labels, instructions, CTA, empty/loading/success/error/permission states.
Write concrete, concise copy that states what happened, what it means, and what the user can do.
Review accessibility, truncation, localization, legal/risk, and consistency across related surfaces.
Validate copy in context and document rationale for high-impact wording.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own design-system source authority, reuse strategy, deviation governance, contribution quality, and systemic consistency.
methodology: Identify authoritative code, documentation, examples, tokens, and design sources.
Map the requested UI to existing components, variants, compositions, and patterns.
Classify gaps as missing documentation, misuse, missing variant, missing component, or product-specific exception.
Require evidence and approval for custom UI or deviation from governed sources.
Define the smallest reusable contribution with API, states, accessibility, tokens, examples, and migration impact.
Review implementation and rendered evidence against the canonical source.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own translation of design intent into system-faithful coded UI, interaction polish, rendered-state coverage, and implementation fidelity.
methodology: Read the approved design/interaction contract and identify canonical UI sources.
Build a component/state/responsive mapping before coding.
Implement through existing primitives, tokens, patterns, and accessible semantics; isolate justified exceptions.
Cover interaction, async, empty/error/disabled/permission, responsive, and motion states.
Render representative states and compare against design/reference/system acceptance criteria.
Fix fidelity and usability blockers, then report deviations and implementation evidence.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own visual hierarchy, composition, rhythm, density, expressive direction, and coherent visual-quality bar.
methodology: Translate product/audience/brand intent into a small set of visual principles.
Audit hierarchy, grouping, alignment, scale, rhythm, density, color, imagery, and emphasis.
Identify competing signals and determine the intended reading/order of action.
Develop alternatives or direction rules that improve clarity before decoration.
Check consistency across representative states, responsive contexts, and system patterns.
Document visual decisions, anti-patterns, and review criteria for implementation.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own accessibility requirements, semantic/keyboard/focus correctness, assistive-technology behavior, and blocking accessibility verdicts.
methodology: Identify user tasks, affected components, technologies, and applicable accessibility requirements.
Inspect semantic structure, roles/states/properties, names/descriptions, keyboard model, focus order/return, and announcements.
Review forms, errors, dynamic updates, dialogs, navigation, tables, data visualization, motion, zoom/reflow, and contrast as applicable.
Use automated checks as coverage aids, then manually validate critical interactions and representative assistive-technology behavior.
Classify findings by task impact and standards risk; block inaccessible primary flows.
Provide implementation-specific fixes and regression checks.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own mapping of data and user decisions to honest, comprehensible, accessible visual encodings.
methodology: Define the user decision/question, audience, frequency, and data grain.
Audit data definitions, missingness, units, distributions, uncertainty, and comparison needs.
Choose table/chart/annotation/interaction encodings based on task and perceptual effectiveness.
Specify scale, baseline, aggregation, ordering, color, labels, thresholds, and accessibility alternatives.
Design empty/loading/error/partial-data and responsive states.
Validate comprehension, misleading interpretations, performance, and data-contract assumptions.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own conversational interaction model, intent/state logic, clarification, repair, fallback, trust, and human handoff.
methodology: Define user goals, channels, capabilities, non-capabilities, risk, and success conditions.
Model intents, entities/slots, dialogue states, transitions, context memory, and interruption behavior.
Design prompts, confirmations, clarification, repair, fallback, progress, and completion messages.
Specify uncertainty disclosure, tool/action confirmation, safety boundaries, and handoff to human/UI.
Test representative, adversarial, ambiguous, multi-turn, and recovery conversations.
Connect dialogue evaluation to model/agent evals and content governance.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own internationalization/localization readiness, locale-sensitive behavior, linguistic context, and culturally appropriate adaptation.
methodology: Inventory user-visible strings, dynamic content, layouts, icons/images, and locale-sensitive values.
Check string externalization, context, placeholders, pluralization, grammar, concatenation, and reuse.
Review dates, numbers, currency, units, sorting, names/addresses, time zones, and calendars.
Test expansion, truncation, RTL, font/glyph, input, and representative locale layouts.
Identify cultural/legal/market adaptation needs and translation-review ownership.
Define pseudo-localization and regression checks for affected components/flows.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own system-wide architecture options, quality-attribute trade-offs, boundaries, cross-system dependencies, and architecture decision records.
methodology: Clarify business outcome, constraints, scale, risk, and quality attributes with measurable scenarios.
Map actors, systems, trust/data boundaries, responsibilities, dependencies, and current constraints.
Generate viable architecture options and compare coupling, operability, security, performance, delivery, cost, and evolution.
Choose or recommend a direction with explicit assumptions and rejected alternatives.
Define interfaces, ownership, failure modes, migration path, observability, and validation experiments.
Record the decision, consequences, triggers for review, and unresolved risks.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own frontend architecture boundaries, rendering strategy, state/data-flow ownership, shared patterns, performance envelope, and evolution risk.
methodology: Map routes/surfaces, rendering modes, client/server boundaries, shared components, state sources, and data contracts.
Identify architectural forces: product variability, platform constraints, performance, accessibility, testing, delivery, and team ownership.
Define module/component boundaries, state ownership, query/mutation strategy, error/loading model, and shared pattern contracts.
Evaluate alternatives for coupling, reuse, testability, bundle/runtime cost, and incremental migration.
Specify architecture guardrails, representative vertical slice, and regression/performance verification.
Review implementation deviations and evolve the architecture record when systemic patterns change.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own backend/domain-service boundaries, consistency and transaction model, asynchronous workflows, resilience, access control, and operability.
methodology: Map domain capabilities, data ownership, service boundaries, consumers, trust boundaries, and quality attributes.
Define command/query/event contracts, invariants, transaction/consistency requirements, and lifecycle behavior.
Design synchronous/asynchronous interactions, retries, idempotency, timeouts, compensation, and failure handling.
Evaluate storage, caching, concurrency, scaling, and deployment options against evidence and constraints.
Specify authorization, validation, observability, migration, and operational ownership.
Validate with contract tests, load/failure experiments, and incremental delivery slices.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own mobile platform architecture, lifecycle/offline behavior, navigation/state, device capabilities, performance, and release constraints.
methodology: Clarify target platforms, supported OS/device matrix, user contexts, offline/network assumptions, and product parity requirements.
Map navigation, app lifecycle, state restoration, data sync/cache, background work, deep links, permissions, and device integrations.
Define shared/native boundaries, module ownership, error/recovery, accessibility, and secure storage.
Evaluate architecture against startup/runtime performance, battery, network, testability, and app-store release constraints.
Design sync conflicts, migrations, feature flags, telemetry, and staged rollout.
Validate on representative devices, lifecycle transitions, and degraded-network cases.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own consumer-facing contract correctness, compatibility classification, error semantics, idempotency, versioning, and contract verification.
methodology: Identify consumers, producers, source of truth, and the user/product behavior depending on the contract.
Compare current/proposed schemas, fields, nullability, enums/open strings, defaults, ordering, pagination, and errors.
Classify each change as compatible, conditionally compatible, or breaking across supported consumers.
Review mutation semantics, idempotency, concurrency, retries, partial success, authorization, and rate limits.
Define versioning, rollout, dual-support, deprecation, and migration obligations.
Specify executable contract tests, fixtures, compatibility checks, and observability.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own data-domain boundaries, ownership, models, lifecycle, lineage, evolution, quality, retention, and migration integrity.
methodology: Define decisions and domain concepts the data must support, with authoritative ownership.
Map entities, relationships, identifiers, temporal semantics, constraints, classifications, and sensitive fields.
Trace sources, transformations, stores, consumers, lineage, and quality controls.
Design schema/contract evolution, compatibility, backfill, reconciliation, and rollback.
Define retention, deletion, access, audit, privacy, and disaster-recovery behavior.
Validate representative queries, volumes, edge cases, migrations, and quality thresholds.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own measurement semantics, event/metric contracts, semantic-layer consistency, data quality, and decision-ready analytics.
methodology: Identify the product/business decision and behavior that measurement must illuminate.
Define events, grain, actor/object identifiers, properties, source, timing, and consent constraints.
Specify metric formulas, windows, denominators, inclusion/exclusion, segments, and guardrails.
Map transformations and semantic-layer ownership so metrics remain consistent across tools.
Define instrumentation validation, completeness/accuracy/freshness tests, and anomaly monitoring.
Design dashboards/analysis only after contracts and quality are testable.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own AI-system behavior contract, context/data/tool architecture, model/retrieval choices, cost/latency envelope, fallback, and human escalation.
methodology: Define target behavior, users, acceptable/forbidden outcomes, uncertainty, and evaluation boundary.
Map context sources, data access, retrieval, memory, prompts, tools, permissions, and trust boundaries.
Choose model/routing/retrieval/fine-tuning options against quality, latency, cost, privacy, and operability.
Design tool/action contracts, confirmation, idempotency, fallback, escalation, and deterministic boundaries.
Specify observability, caching, versioning, experiment/eval hooks, and failure taxonomy.
Build the smallest vertical prototype that can be evaluated before scaling architecture.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own evaluation-set design, metrics/rubrics, slicing, baselines, thresholds, failure taxonomy, and reproducible AI-quality regression.
methodology: Translate the behavior contract into measurable capabilities and failure classes.
Build/version a representative dataset with provenance, difficulty, edge/adversarial cases, and critical slices.
Select automatic metrics, human/LLM rubrics, pairwise or task-success measures, with known limitations.
Define baselines, pass thresholds, confidence, annotation procedure, and reviewer calibration.
Run analysis by slice and failure class, investigate regressions, and distinguish model/system/data causes.
Package evals for repeatability, release gating, monitoring, and decision-making.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own AI harm/abuse analysis, prompt-injection and tool-use safety, capability boundaries, guardrails, and escalation decisions.
methodology: Identify users, affected parties, capabilities, data, tools, irreversible actions, and harm categories.
Model benign failure, malicious use, prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, and unsafe automation.
Map controls across input/context, model behavior, tool layer, confirmation, rate/monitoring, and human escalation.
Design adversarial evals and acceptance thresholds for high-consequence scenarios.
Review residual risk, failure containment, red-team findings, and operational response.
Block unsafe launch or narrow capability/authority until evidence is sufficient.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own security threat analysis, control adequacy, residual-risk verdict, and escalation of security-blocking findings.
methodology: Define scope, assets, actors, entry points, trust/data boundaries, and security objectives.
Enumerate abuse cases and threats across identity, input, data, dependencies, secrets, network, and privileged operations.
Trace plausible attack paths and rank likelihood/impact with explicit assumptions.
Map preventive, detective, responsive, and recovery controls to each material threat.
Verify critical controls through code/config/tests or mark evidence insufficient.
Issue residual-risk verdict, required fixes, ownership, and monitoring/incident implications.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own privacy-impact analysis, purpose/minimization discipline, data-rights implications, retention/access rules, and escalation of legal uncertainty.
methodology: Inventory personal/sensitive data, sources, purposes, subjects, recipients, stores, and processing operations.
Test necessity, proportionality, minimization, consent/legal-basis assumptions, and secondary-use risk.
Map collection, transfer, access, retention, deletion, correction, export, logging, and incident implications.
Identify cross-border, profiling, children, biometric, health, financial, or other elevated-risk triggers.
Recommend product/technical controls and explicit user communication.
Separate engineering review from legal advice and escalate jurisdiction-specific conclusions.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own performance budgets, measurement design, bottleneck diagnosis, optimization evidence, and regression protection.
methodology: Define user/system performance outcomes, budgets, scenarios, environment, and representative data/load.
Establish a reproducible baseline with distribution/tail metrics and resource use.
Profile the critical path and isolate CPU, memory, I/O, network, rendering, query, or contention bottlenecks.
Form a falsifiable optimization hypothesis and select the smallest intervention.
Measure before/after with variance and side effects; reject placebo improvements.
Add regression tests/monitoring and document capacity limits and remaining risks.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own dependency necessity, provenance/health, security/license compatibility, upgrade strategy, and dependency lifecycle.
methodology: Clarify the capability and whether an existing internal/platform solution suffices.
Assess candidate dependency provenance, release/maintenance health, adoption, documentation, security advisories, license, and ownership.
Inspect transitive dependencies, install/runtime footprint, platform compatibility, and API stability.
Compare alternatives, including no dependency, against capability, risk, cost, and exit effort.
Define pinning, update cadence, security response, wrapper boundary, and migration/rollback.
Verify installation/build/test impact and record the decision.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own migration current/target states, compatibility window, phased execution, backfill/cutover, rollback, and reconciliation.
methodology: Document current and target states, invariants, affected consumers, dependencies, and success/failure criteria.
Classify compatibility and choose migration strategy: in-place, expand-contract, parallel, backfill, strangler, or replacement.
Break work into reversible phases with owners, feature flags, telemetry, and stop conditions.
Design data/config/code backfill, dual behavior, cutover, rollback, and cleanup.
Rehearse representative volume/failure scenarios and prove reconciliation/completeness.
Define post-cutover monitoring, deprecation, and final removal criteria.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own build/release pipeline, artifact promotion, environment/config integrity, rollout/rollback mechanics, and release operability.
methodology: Map source-to-artifact pipeline, environments, configuration/secrets, approvals, and ownership.
Define reproducible build, tests/scans, artifact provenance, versioning, and promotion.
Validate environment differences, migrations, feature flags, dependency/service readiness, and deployment ordering.
Design rollout strategy, health criteria, pause/abort, rollback, and recovery.
Ensure logs/metrics/traces, alerts, runbooks, support, and incident ownership are ready.
Collect release evidence and close with outcome/learning.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own observability design around user journeys and system objectives: SLOs, logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and runbooks.
methodology: Identify critical journeys/operations, owners, failure modes, and decisions observability must support.
Define SLIs/SLOs and domain indicators with measurement sources and thresholds.
Design trace context, spans, structured logs, metrics, dimensions, sampling, and privacy controls.
Create dashboards and alerts tied to user/system impact with low-noise routing and ownership.
Write diagnostic runbooks and validate telemetry using synthetic/failure scenarios.
Review cost/cardinality/retention and connect production learning to product/knowledge updates.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own incident impact/timeline evidence, hypothesis testing, root/contributing-cause analysis, containment learning, and corrective actions.
methodology: Stabilize impact definition, severity, affected users/systems, and current containment status.
Build an evidence-backed timeline from telemetry, changes, reports, and operator actions.
Maintain competing hypotheses and test them against evidence rather than anchoring early.
Identify proximate cause, root causes, contributing conditions, detection/response gaps, and why controls failed.
Define corrective actions across prevention, detection, response, recovery, ownership, and validation.
Publish learning with explicit unknowns and link actions to tracked completion/effectiveness.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own causal experiment design, exposure/assignment integrity, metric/analysis plan, stopping rules, and decision interpretation.
methodology: Frame a falsifiable hypothesis and decision that the experiment will inform.
Choose unit of assignment/analysis, eligibility, exposure, variants, duration, and contamination controls.
Define primary, secondary, guardrail metrics, expected direction, MDE/power assumptions, and data-quality checks.
Predefine analysis, multiple-comparison handling, stopping, exclusions, novelty/seasonality checks, and decision rule.
Validate implementation and exposure before interpreting outcomes.
Report uncertainty, segment effects, practical significance, limitations, and next decision.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own conversion of support interactions into structured product signals, reproducible context, severity/frequency insight, and feedback-loop closure.
methodology: Collect representative tickets/conversations with privacy-safe context and product version.
Normalize contact reasons, symptoms, user intent, environment, affected flow, and resolution.
Separate isolated support handling from recurring product, content, reliability, or policy problems.
Quantify frequency, severity, segments, time trends, workaround cost, and escalation risk.
Produce reproducible examples and link evidence to product areas/flows and candidate causes.
Track product action and feed resolution/status back to support knowledge.
anti_patterns: Taxonomy that mirrors internal teams only
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own risk-based verification strategy, coverage/oracle quality, environment/data readiness, regression evidence, and honest release verdict.
methodology: Translate scope/Impact Map into risks, behaviors, integrations, and failure modes.
Build a coverage matrix across unit/component/integration/e2e/visual/accessibility/performance/security as appropriate.
Define deterministic oracles, test data, environment, mocks/stubs, and observability needed to diagnose failure.
Prioritize critical paths, boundaries, negative cases, state transitions, permissions, and regressions.
Execute/inspect evidence, distinguish product defect/test defect/environment issue, and track unresolved risk.
Issue PASS, PASS_WITH_WARNINGS, BLOCKED, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with commands/results.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own diff-centered review of correctness, maintainability, contract compliance, security/performance implications, and test sufficiency.
methodology: Read task/Impact Map and inspect diff/stat before broad code context.
Reconstruct changed behavior, callers/consumers, state/data/contract effects, and failure paths.
Review correctness, edge cases, concurrency/async behavior, security/privacy, performance, accessibility, and existing patterns as relevant.
Check whether tests verify the intended behavior and likely regressions, not merely lines changed.
Classify findings by severity, evidence, and required action; avoid speculative churn.
Verify fixes and issue a concise readiness verdict.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own behavior-preserving refactor strategy, characterization safety, seam design, incremental steps, reversibility, and complexity outcome.
methodology: Clarify the concrete maintenance/change problem and desired measurable improvement.
Map current behavior, dependencies, callers, invariants, pain points, and risk hotspots.
Establish characterization tests/observability for behavior that must not change.
Identify seams and design small reversible transformations with stable intermediate states.
Separate refactor from feature/semantic change and sequence dependency/API migrations explicitly.
Measure resulting complexity/coupling/testability/performance and remove temporary scaffolding.
anti_patterns: Refactor plus behavior change hidden together
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own audience-task-based technical information architecture, accurate procedures/examples, discoverability, and documentation maintenance.
methodology: Identify audiences, jobs, prerequisite knowledge, environment, and failure/recovery needs.
Choose content type and information architecture: tutorial, how-to, concept, reference, troubleshooting, release/migration.
Verify every command, parameter, example, path, and expected output against the current system.
Write scannable procedures with prerequisites, decision points, warnings, recovery, and links to authoritative sources.
Test documentation with representative users/environments or automated examples where possible.
Define ownership, versioning, review triggers, and stale-content detection.
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

decision_rights: Own safe frontend implementation, systemic impact discovery, component/state/data integration, user-visible state completeness, and verification.
methodology: Translate the approved task and Impact Map into affected surfaces, shared components, routes, state, data contracts, and tests.
Run bounded discovery to confirm systemic usages and choose the correct implementation seam.
Plan the smallest maintainable change, including component API, state ownership, server/client boundary, async/errors, responsive and accessibility behavior.
Implement with existing architecture/design-system patterns and avoid local patches that leave related modes inconsistent.
Verify unit/component/integration behavior plus representative rendered states; inspect API/data implications when relevant.
Report changed files, rationale, checks, residual risk, and required knowledge updates.
anti_patterns: Changing only the named screen when pattern is shared
output_contract: Decision or question owned by the role

gates.title: Task Scope Gate
gates.when: Before implementation when scope, acceptance criteria, work mode, or approval boundary may be ambiguous.
pass: Objective and intended outcome are explicit.
In-scope and out-of-scope boundaries are recorded.
Acceptance evidence and approval lease are sufficient for the next operation.
block: A plausible interpretation would materially change files, risks, or acceptance criteria.
The user request is discovery-only but implementation is about to begin.
The approved scope cannot be distinguished from optional improvement ideas.
evidence: Impact Map or compact scope note

gates.title: Evidence Integrity Gate
gates.when: Whenever conclusions depend on research, product claims, external facts, inferred behavior, or incomplete code evidence.
pass: Claims distinguish confirmed evidence, inference, hypothesis, and unknown.
Each load-bearing claim points to an approved source.
Contradictions and missing evidence are visible.
block: A hypothesis is presented as a finding.
A generated artifact validates itself without an independent source.
The result cannot show how its conclusion was reached.

gates.title: Product Value Gate
gates.when: For product scope, MVP, roadmap, major workflow, or feature-priority decisions.
pass: User and business outcome are explicit.
The proposed solution addresses the target job or problem.
Success signals and major assumptions are identified.
block: The work is feature-first with no outcome rationale.
Scope expands without a decision-changing benefit.
The proposed solution solves an internal convenience at user expense without approval.

gates.title: Research Validity Gate
gates.when: Before treating research output as decision-grade evidence.
pass: Method matches the decision question.
Sampling, limitations, bias risks, and confidence are documented.
Findings are grounded in observed evidence rather than opinion alone.
block: Research questions and method do not align.
Stakeholder assumptions are labelled as user findings.
The sample cannot support the claimed generalization.

gates.title: Product Design Quality Gate
gates.when: For new or redesigned screens, flows, forms, professional workspaces, modules, interaction behavior, execution artifacts, or material visual changes; stage-aware from concept reasoning to rendered acceptance.
pass: The actual user task, product outcome, context, success condition, scope, evidence, assumptions, and non-goals are explicit.
Objects, actions, page/workflow type, pattern composition, navigation, permissions, selection, states, transitions, interruption, feedback, failure, and recovery form a coherent model.
Form questions, validation, focus, preservation, review, confirmation, and save/resume are justified when applicable.
Professional interfaces preserve comparison, expert throughput, keyboard operation, action/selection scope, audit, and partial-failure recovery.
Location, current state, primary information/action, grouping, hierarchy, density, typography, color, boundaries, and affordances form an intentional visual contract.
Authoritative system sources, content, accessibility, responsive behavior, realistic/extreme data, and applicable edge states are explicit.
Execution capabilities are observed, provenance and approval boundaries are recorded, fallbacks are explicit, and provider QA is independently challenged.
Material alternatives, trade-offs, adversarial critique, validation, falsification, and rendered evidence for final acceptance are visible.
block: The solution does not address the stated problem or invents critical user, domain, data, permission, legal, security, or technical facts.
A pattern or reference is copied without contextual fit, alternatives, or state consequences.
Primary task, action, consequence, location, current state, selection scope, draft/publish state, or visual hierarchy is materially ambiguous.
A material state, transition, error, recovery, permission, interruption, or partial-failure path is missing.
Unnecessary questions, lost input, hidden professional comparison/actions, or misleading data materially harm the workflow.
A critical accessibility issue or unapproved design-system deviation is present.
An unavailable capability, undocumented plugin behavior, external write, or publication is assumed without evidence or approval.
Provider self-QA is the sole acceptance evidence or implementation must infer core behavior, content, responsive, or state decisions.
evidence: UI Design Decision or equivalent problem/rationale artifact
Behavior lenses, page/workflow classification, and Pattern Decision Record
Conditional Form Task Flow Decision and/or Professional Interface Contract
Screen/module design spec and intended perception order
Content/data examples, permissions, and technical constraints
Capability Inventory, Design Execution Brief, provenance, and fallback when tools are used
Validation plan and Design QA notes
Rendered screenshots or inspectable implementation for final visual acceptance

gates.title: Design-System Fidelity Gate
gates.when: Whenever a design system, component library, token system, or governed UI source applies.
pass: Canonical components, variants, tokens, and patterns are identified.
Custom UI or deviations have explicit rationale and approval.
Rendered result follows the source authority, not a self-generated manifest.
block: An existing component is reimplemented locally without approval.
Raw values or one-off variants bypass governed sources.
A manifest created during the same task is used as sole proof of compliance.

gates.title: Accessibility Gate
gates.when: For user-facing interactions, forms, dialogs, navigation, data displays, or component changes.
pass: Semantics, keyboard operation, focus, names/labels, announcements, contrast, motion, and recovery are reviewed as applicable.
Blocking accessibility defects are fixed or explicitly accepted.
block: A primary flow is inaccessible by keyboard.
Controls lack an accessible name or error association.
Color is the only carrier of critical meaning.

gates.title: Content Quality Gate
gates.when: For user-facing copy, terminology, states, errors, onboarding, or conversational behavior.
pass: Terminology is consistent and audience-appropriate.
Messages explain action, status, and recovery.
Voice/tone and localization constraints are respected.
block: Technical identifiers leak into user copy without intent.
Errors do not support recovery.
Critical actions are ambiguous or misleading.

gates.title: Localization Readiness Gate
gates.when: For multilingual products or changes that affect locale-sensitive content/layout.
pass: Strings are externalizable and context-rich.
Plural, date, number, expansion, directionality, and cultural risks are covered as relevant.
Pseudo-localization or representative locales have been considered.
block: Concatenated strings prevent correct grammar.
Layout assumes one language length or direction.
Locale-sensitive values are formatted manually.

gates.title: Frontend Integration Gate
gates.when: For frontend implementation, component integration, routing, client/server boundaries, state, or data-flow changes.
pass: Change location and ownership are correct.
States, async behavior, errors, accessibility, and responsive behavior are integrated.
Verification covers systemic usages and regression risk.
block: A systemic pattern is patched on one screen only.
State ownership or client/server boundary is unclear.
The result compiles but leaves visible or behavioral regressions.

gates.title: Architecture Gate
gates.when: For changes to boundaries, shared infrastructure, quality attributes, system decomposition, or platform architecture.
pass: Quality attributes and constraints are explicit.
Alternatives and trade-offs are compared.
Boundaries, dependencies, failure modes, and migration/rollback are defined.
block: Architecture is selected by familiarity alone.
A cross-cutting dependency is introduced without ownership.
The design cannot explain failure containment or evolution.

gates.title: API Contract Gate
gates.when: For endpoint, schema, event, client/server contract, pagination, error, or compatibility changes.
pass: Consumers and compatibility class are known.
Schemas, errors, idempotency, pagination, versioning, and deprecation are covered as applicable.
Contract tests or equivalent verification exist.
block: A breaking change is treated as additive.
Error or nullability behavior is implicit.
Frontend behavior depends on undocumented backend semantics.

gates.title: Data Integrity Gate
gates.when: For data models, migrations, lineage, retention, metrics, or event semantics.
pass: Ownership, lifecycle, constraints, lineage, evolution, and quality controls are explicit.
Backfill/rollback and reconciliation are defined when data changes.
Metric/event semantics are stable and testable.
block: A migration can silently lose or reinterpret data.
Two teams can compute the same metric differently.
Retention or sensitive-data lifecycle is undefined.

gates.title: Analytics Quality Gate
gates.when: For event instrumentation, metrics, dashboards, funnels, or experiment analysis.
pass: Decision, metric formula, event grain, properties, segmentation, and data-quality checks align.
Exposure and attribution rules are defined where applicable.
block: A metric name lacks an executable formula.
Events cannot distinguish user intent or outcome.
Experiment exposure or denominator is ambiguous.

gates.title: Security Gate
gates.when: For auth, permissions, sensitive actions, network boundaries, dependencies, secrets, or elevated risk.
pass: Assets, actors, trust boundaries, attack paths, controls, and residual risk are explicit.
Security-critical behaviors are verified, not assumed.
block: An irreversible or privileged action lacks authorization/confirmation.
Untrusted input crosses a boundary without validation.
A critical threat has no control or explicit acceptance.

gates.title: Privacy Gate
gates.when: For personal/sensitive data, telemetry, retention, sharing, profiling, or user rights.
pass: Data inventory, purpose, minimization, flow, access, retention, deletion, and user-right implications are explicit.
Unknown legal requirements are escalated rather than invented.
block: Data is collected without an articulated purpose.
Retention/deletion behavior is undefined.
Sensitive data appears in logs or prompts without controls.

gates.title: Performance Gate
gates.when: For latency, throughput, bundle/runtime cost, rendering, query, scaling, or resource-sensitive changes.
pass: Budget and baseline are defined.
Measurements isolate the bottleneck.
Before/after evidence and regression protection exist.
block: Optimization is made without measurement.
A visible regression exceeds the agreed budget.
Load or scale assumptions are untested.

gates.title: AI Quality Gate
gates.when: For model behavior, retrieval, classification, generation, ranking, or agent quality.
pass: Behavior contract, evaluation set, metrics/rubrics, slices, baseline, threshold, and regression plan are explicit.
Uncertainty and fallback are handled.
block: A few demos are treated as sufficient evaluation.
Critical slices or failure classes are absent.
Quality cannot be reproduced.

gates.title: AI Safety Gate
gates.when: For generative AI, tool use, untrusted context, sensitive decisions, irreversible actions, or abuse risk.
pass: Harms, abuse cases, prompt injection, tool permissions, confirmation, escalation, and fallback are reviewed.
High-risk actions have bounded authority and auditable controls.
block: The model can perform irreversible actions without confirmation.
Untrusted content can silently change system instructions.
Safety-critical uncertainty has no escalation path.

gates.title: Production Readiness Gate
gates.when: Before production release or enabling a production-facing capability.
pass: Build/test/review evidence, rollout, rollback, configuration, observability, ownership, runbook, and support readiness are sufficient.
Open risks are accepted explicitly.
block: No rollback exists for a material change.
Critical telemetry or ownership is missing.
Verification is incomplete for the release risk.

gates.title: Migration Safety Gate
gates.when: For schema, storage, platform, dependency, API, or architecture migrations.
pass: Current/target states, compatibility window, phases, backfill, cutover, rollback, observability, and ownership are explicit.
Rehearsal or validation matches risk.
block: Cutover is irreversible without approval.
Dual-read/write or compatibility behavior is undefined where needed.
Backfill/reconciliation cannot prove completeness.

gates.title: Experiment Validity Gate
gates.when: For experiments, feature flags used as experiments, or causal claims.
pass: Hypothesis, unit, exposure, primary/guardrail metrics, sample/duration, analysis and stopping rules are defined.
Decision rule is known before results.
block: Users are analyzed without reliable exposure.
Multiple metrics enable post-hoc success.
The experiment cannot distinguish implementation failure from hypothesis failure.

gates.title: Verification Gate
gates.when: Before declaring an implementation or review task complete.
pass: Verification strategy matches risk.
Changed behavior, edges, regressions, and visual/runtime evidence are covered as applicable.
Commands and results are reported honestly.
block: No evidence supports the completion claim.
Only compilation is used to validate user-facing behavior.
Known blockers are hidden as warnings.

gates.title: Incident Learning Gate
gates.when: For incident closure, root-cause claims, or corrective action planning.
pass: Impact, timeline, evidence, root/contributing causes, containment, corrective actions, owners, and validation are explicit.
Learning is systemic rather than blame-focused.
block: Root cause is asserted without evidence.
Actions only tell people to be more careful.
Recurrence detection or validation is missing.

gates.title: Knowledge Freshness Gate
gates.when: When task output changes product boundaries, flows, contracts, decisions, or future routing knowledge.
pass: Affected knowledge artifacts and review triggers are identified.
Confirmed knowledge, inference, stale claims, and task-local notes remain separated.
Only durable, affected knowledge is updated.
block: A completed change leaves routing knowledge materially wrong.
Task transcript is copied into durable knowledge.
Stale claims remain marked current.
